media/carousel.notes:
```tsx
<Carousel perView={2} m:color="brand-orange" prevIcon={arrowLeft} nextIcon={arrowRight} labels={{ previous: "Earlier", next: "Later", slide: (n) => `Photo ${n}` }}>{slides}</Carousel>
<Carousel dots={(i) => i + 1} arrows={false} smooth={false}>{slides}</Carousel>
```
media/carousel.a11y:
A labelled `section` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`. The track is focusable (arrow keys scroll it); the
previous / next buttons and the dots are labelled buttons ("Previous", "Next", "Slide n", translated); the active dot
is marked. The buttons sit at the inline edges and mirror in right-to-left layouts.

media/corner-mark.a11y:
Decorative by default (`aria-hidden`): say what it means in the name of the tile ("Video: …"). With `label` it is
`role="img"` with that name. It never takes pointer events, so the card under it stays clickable. `show="hover"` also
shows on keyboard focus and is always visible on touch screens; reduced motion: no slide.

media/media.notes:
`openMedia(src, { title, kind, alt, poster, size, autoplay, fallback })` returns the dialog's promise (`title` defaults to "Preview", translated).

```tsx
<Media src={url} fallback={<Empty icon={image} title="The photo is gone" />} />
```
media/media.a11y:
Images take `alt` (empty: decorative); video and audio keep native controls (keyboard and screen reader friendly).
A failed load is announced as a status message. Images load lazily and decode off the main thread.

media/overlay.notes:
```tsx
<Overlay effect="spotlight" m:color="brand-orange" />

```

`quietMedia()` is true on save-data, 2G or reduced motion.
media/overlay.a11y:
Decorative by default: `aria-hidden`, inert, no pointer events (clicks reach the content underneath). Video and
canvas pause off screen and stay still with reduced motion; the canvas loop runs on the motion engine's clock
("pause all" and the global speed reach it). Position and size are CSS variables set through CSSOM (CSP safe).

media/picture.notes: Other attributes (`draggable`, `id`, `data-*`…) pass to the image. For video, audio or a preview dialog use Media.
media/picture.a11y:
`alt` is always written: the text of the picture, or empty for decoration. The fallback keeps the alternative text as
its accessible name. Width and height keep the layout still while the image loads.
